skill.name: d3js-visualization
skill.description: Create interactive D3.js charts, reusable visualization templates, and responsive browser examples for custom data visualization work.
skill.summary: Create interactive D3.js charts, templates, and examples for browser data visualization.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from JavaScript template literals, Markdown fences, identifiers named key, CSS grid text, and chart logic. The review confirms low-risk CDN script usage in examples and one medium browser XSS risk from raw tooltip HTML rendering. No prompt injection, credential access, shell execution, or malware intent was found.

remediation.issue: Tooltip helpers and examples render raw HTML content.
remediation.suggestion: Use text() for untrusted values, build tooltip DOM nodes safely, or sanitize content before calling html().

remediation.issue: Examples load D3 from a remote CDN script tag.
remediation.suggestion: For production use, install d3 locally or pin CDN assets with Subresource Integrity and a Content Security Policy.

content.value_statement: Custom browser charts often require many D3 decisions before any data appears. This skill supplies chart guidance, templates, helpers, and examples for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose D3.js instead of simpler chart libraries.
Provides reusable line, bar, scatter, and pie chart template patterns.
Includes data parsing, statistics, grouping, and cleaning helper guidance.
Shows complete line chart, bar chart, and network graph browser examples.
Covers responsive SVG, axes, transitions, tooltips, and accessibility patterns.
Documents integration approaches for React, Vue, Angular, and Svelte.
limitations: It targets browser-based D3.js work, not server-side image rendering.
Examples use generated or local data, so users must adapt real data loading.
Some snippets use CDN scripts and HTML tooltips that need production hardening.
The repository does not include an automated test suite or build pipeline.

use_cases.title: Create an Interactive Dashboard Chart
use_cases.description: Build a custom chart with axes, responsive sizing, transitions, and tooltip behavior for a dashboard view.

use_cases.title: Prepare Data for Visual Analysis
use_cases.description: Transform CSV-style data into grouped, aggregated, and typed structures before rendering a visualization.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Network Visualization
use_cases.description: Use force-directed graph patterns to explore relationships, node groups, hover states, and interactive controls.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Chart Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the best D3.js chart type for this dataset and goal: [describe data and audience]. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Responsive Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive D3.js chart plan for [data shape]. Include scales, axes, margin convention, interactions, and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the reusable D3 template for [line, bar, scatter, or pie]. Include needed configuration, data accessors, and update behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Visualization
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced D3.js visualization for [complex dataset]. Include performance strategy, interaction model, data transformation, and production risks.

output_examples.input: Create a responsive time-series chart for monthly revenue.
output: A chart plan using time scales, a line generator, clear axes, and hover details.
A responsiveness plan using container width, viewBox sizing, and debounced resize handling.
A checklist for accessibility labels, contrast, and keyboard support.

output_examples.input: Compare sales across three products and support grouped or stacked views.
output: A bar chart design with band scales, grouped and stacked modes, and animated transitions.
A legend interaction model for toggling product visibility.
A tooltip content plan that avoids unsafe HTML for untrusted labels.

output_examples.input: Show relationships between teams, projects, and dependencies.
output: A force-directed network plan with node sizing, group coloring, drag behavior, and hover highlighting.
A performance note covering simulation parameters and update frequency.
A usability note for zoom, pan, labels, and summary statistics.

best_practices: Start with the chart selection guide before writing D3 code.
Use stable data joins and key functions for predictable updates.
Test charts with real data sizes, long labels, and small viewports.
anti_patterns: Using D3.js for simple charts that a smaller chart library can handle.
Rendering untrusted values through HTML tooltips without sanitization.
Redrawing every element on each interaction when data joins can update only changed elements.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create custom D3.js charts, reusable templates, data helpers, and interactive browser visualizations.

faq.question: Does it include working examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes line chart, bar chart, and network graph examples that run in a browser.

faq.question: Can it help choose the right chart?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for time series, comparisons, relationships, distributions, and network data.

faq.question: Does it support frontend frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. The references discuss integration patterns for React, Vue, Angular, and Svelte.

faq.question: Is it production ready by default?
faq.answer: No. Production use should add data validation, safer tooltip rendering, dependency pinning, and project tests.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
